_comment: R7-01. Every vanilla thing gets one action: keep (vanilla function and vanilla art; menial things), restyle (vanilla function, the mod's art at vanilla's 16 px), replace (gone; a mod thing does its job, named in 'with'), remove (unreachable). Rules are ordered; the first match wins. 'by' says who decided: Champ, the GDD, or PROPOSED (Claude's call, waiting for Champ; the R6 or R7 item it comes from in brackets). Round 6 is PROPOSED too, so an R6 item never decides by itself; where Champ made the call and Claude the staging, the label says both. Ids are vanilla ids without 'minecraft:'; globs and #tags work. kind 'content' means item and block. Potions are one id per content: potion@strength. Spawn eggs and mob buckets follow their mob. An entity replace rule may name convert_to: that mob becomes the mod entity in place. tool_stand_ins: a mod item that does a removed vanilla tool's job (the drops that need that tool). After any change run: python tools/vanilla_scope.py --orphans, then --datapack src/generated/scope --lock.
_milestone_note: milestone: the build the generated pack is for (bump it when a milestone starts, then rerun --datapack and --lock). target_milestone: where the plan must be complete; --check tests every milestone in between. A rule's 'from' (default M1) is the milestone it starts at.
_empty_trade_levels_note: PROPOSED (R7-01; decide list item 5). A villager level the trade rewrite empties (the cleric's 3, the mason's and weaponsmith's 5; from M3 the armorer's 4 and 5) adds no offer when a villager reaches it ('empty'). 'lower' makes it roll the stocked lower level with the most trades instead, which repeats offers the villager already holds: certainly for every one but the mason's level 5 (about 1 in 8 there). A level 1 left empty always fails --check.

grass_seeds.source: short grass sometimes drops a carrot (2%), a potato (2%) or beetroot seeds (3%) when broken without shears, as it drops wheat seeds; town farmers also sell seed stock. Until M5 village farms and zombies supply them

fern_dye.source: fern -> green dye (cactus goes with the deserts at M5)

mushroom_dye.source: brown mushroom -> brown dye (cha-iro, tea brown); cocoa goes with the jungles at M5

bone_block_cutting.source: bone block -> 3 bone at the stonecutter (fossils keep generating bone blocks). Skeletons go at M3; until M5 structure chests still hold bones

black_powder.source: black powder: charcoal + sulfur (26.3's sulfur caves) -> 2 gunpowder, for hanabi. Creepers and witches go at M3; until M5 structure chests still hold gunpowder

natagumo_webs.source: the Natagumo region, Rui's spider mountain [canon], generates webs; cutting one with the blade gives string, shearing it gives the web (regional: one mountain, so it supplies webs, not the world's string)

hemp.source: asa (hemp): wild hemp in plains and forests, a crop; 1 stem -> 2 string. Its leaf is the asanoha pattern of Nezuko's kimono [canon]

#minecraft:swords.why: the sword goes at Build 0; the blade's minecraft:tool component copies the sword's rules (cobweb: correct_for_drops, speed 15; #sword_instantly_mines; #sword_efficient 1.5), so a cobweb cut with it drops string as before

earthen walls (tsuchikabe) and earthen bricks; mud comes from water and dirt
